key_insight: Bayesian inference on photoluminescence images can localize where perovskite solar cells degrade, separating interface-driven failure from bulk degradation.
engineering_relevance: This enables targeted stability engineering by identifying which transport-layer interface or device region needs passivation or redesign.
method: Photoluminescence imaging of fully fabricated perovskite solar cells
Drift-diffusion simulations linked to observed images
Bayesian inference used to infer spatial maps of recombination-related parameters during aging
evidence_signal: The authors tracked inferred parameter maps under 70 °C full-spectrum illumination and found pronounced spatial heterogeneity, with the strongest degradation localized at perovskite/transport-layer interfaces.
watch_item: Inferred maps depend on the quality of the physical model and imaging data, so parameter identifiability and model mismatch could affect interpretation.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
